items.title: What do employers usually look at in hiring?

values: 30-minute Shift D paper exercise｜fully fictional

Three alarms: A01 09:10 the simulated panel shows E01 alarm lit, screenshot time verifiable; A02 09:12 transcribed E02 alarm, raw source not attached; A03 09:13 E03 alarm lit but no field report attached. The prompt confirms only these records and cannot confirm a fault.

Two independent load records: L01 E04 09:00 is 120MW and 09:15 is 132MW; L02 E05 at the same two times 80MW and 76MW, all simulated raw readings. T01 is the 09:00 sketch, and current connections and field status are unconfirmed.

Drill rules: the prompt sources for A01, L01, and L02 are given; A02, A03, and T01 are listed as pending. The actual handling or operating approval of all 6 items is unknown, with no capacity, frequency, network constraints, personnel permits, or real system.
Task: three 10-minute blocks

In the first 10 minutes write the 6-row ledger: ID, equipment/object, time, source, known from the prompt, pending, next responsible role. In the middle 10 minutes compute the two load differences and relative changes and classify by the prompt rules; in the last 10 minutes write the pending and handover notes.

Deliver the six-row ledger, the two calculations, the pending cards, and the role handover. Compute only the differences; do not judge overload, do not arrange an operating sequence, and do not connect to real SCADA, EMS, breakers, or dispatch phones.
Reference deliverable (do it independently first)

A01 E01 09:10 screenshot only confirms a signal record; A02 E02 raw source pending; A03 E03 field report pending. L01 E04 is 132−120=12MW, 12/120=10%; L02 E05 is 76−80=−4MW, −4/80=−5%. The two devices are independent; the combined net 8MW cannot be used as an operable or safety basis.

T01 current connections and field status pending. Under the prompt source rule 3 given and 3 pending, 3/6=50% is only the share with sources given; the actual handling approval of all 6 items is unknown. The number of alarms or the differences cannot determine the fault, overload, feasibility of bypass supply, or restoration time.

Hand to the data verification role to supplement A02 raw source and L01/L02 times and units; hand to the field/drawing role to supplement the A03 report and T01 current connections; hand to the authorized lead to verify actual authority and procedures. Names, sign-offs, read-backs, and completion times are all unknown and are not invented.
Self-check rubric｜each item 0–2, 8 points total

Four items: the six IDs correspond to the prompt, the two differences and their percentages are correct, unknowns and the proportional boundary are clear, and evidence supplementation and responsibility handover are complete. Each item 2 = complete and correct, 1 = partial or missing, 0 = wrong or absent. A paper score is not a dispatch qualification.

description.text: Power dispatcher career guide: O*NET/BLS 51-8012 monitoring the grid, load planning, switching orders, and fault handling; verify 2025 US wages and employment, Chinese data boundaries, and paper dispatch exercises.

subject.name: Power Distributors and Dispatchers
subject.summary: Power dispatchers monitor power system status, load, and equipment alarms in the control room, coordinate generation, transmission, and distribution under authorized procedures, handle faults, and record dispatch orders. O*NET 51-8012.00 lists equipment monitoring, switching orders, outage bypass supply, and communication with field personnel as tasks; real control orders must be carried out by authorized personnel under dispatch procedures.
